paper_metadata.title: Quantum alternating operator ansatz with PSO optimizer for portfolio optimization problem

summary: The paper proposes PSO‑optimized QAOAz circuits for portfolio optimization with depth P=5 and evaluates them on 6‑asset portfolios from 2022 market data. On the RP model, PSO‑QAOAz‑RP achieves objective values as low as 3.00×10⁻⁵ with approximate ratios up to 100% across 6 portfolios, outperforming GA, ABC‑LP, and GWO in most cases. On the MV model, PSO‑QAOAz‑MV improves approximate ratios relative to QAOA (≈54.8% average improvement) and QAOAz (≈15.4% improvement) in simulation.

experiments.description: PSO-optimized QAOAz for risk parity (RP) portfolio optimization on six-asset portfolios across Chinese, U.S., European, and emerging markets; compared against GA, ABC-LP, and GWO baselines.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Alternating Operator Ansatz (QAOAz) with ring XY-mixer and PSO classical optimizer
algorithm.ansatz: QAOAz circuit with alternating problem unitary and ring XY-mixer unitary
algorithm.convergence_criteria: max_iterations=10 for PSO; circuit depth fixed at P=5
algorithm.parameter_initialization: PSO particles initialized with random positions and velocities; QAOAz parameters initialized within [0, 2π]

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Binary variable x_i indicates whether asset i is selected; constraint enforces exactly B selected assets
problem_formulation.objective_function: F_RP = sum_{i=1}^n sum_{j=1}^n (x_i (ΣX)_i - x_j (ΣX)_j)^2 + A( sum_{i=1}^n x_i - B )^2
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Cardinality constraint handled by XY-mixer feasibility-preserving subspace; penalty term A(sum x_i - B)^2 appears in formulation but is removed from the problem Hamiltonian and incorporated into the mixer design
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H_p derived from RP objective with Z, ZZ, ZZZ, and ZZZZ terms via x_i=(1+Z_i)/2

problem_instance.description: Portfolio optimization on selected six-stock portfolios from multiple markets
problem_instance.dataset_name: CSI-300 Chinese A-shares, U.S. stocks, European stocks, and emerging market stocks

dataset_specification.description: Portfolios 1-6: six randomly selected CSI-300 stocks each; Portfolios 7-8: AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, NVDA, META and TSLA, JPM, BRK-B, V, JNJ, UNH; Portfolios 9-10: AIR.PA, OR.PA, SAN.PA, DTE.DE, BAS.DE, BMW.DE and VOW3.DE, SIE.DE, ADS.DE, AZN.L, HSBA.L, RIO.L; Portfolios 11-12: EEM, EWZ, FXI, INDA, VWO, RSX and TCEHY, BABA, JD, INFY, PDD, YPF; date range 2022-01-01 to 2022-12-31

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Covariance matrices computed from 2022 market data; six stocks selected per portfolio to fit current quantum hardware limits
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Each algorithm run 10 times; best, worst, average, standard deviation, and approximate ratio reported

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Covariance matrices and expected returns computed from market data; portfolio selection constrained to six assets
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measured bitstrings interpreted as binary asset-selection vectors; objective values and approximate ratios computed from sampled solutions

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: convergence evaluated on Portfolio 1; 10 PSO iterations deemed sufficient

speedup_claims.factor: PSO-QAOAz-RP outperforms GA, ABC-LP, and GWO on most portfolios; best AR up to 100.00%
speedup_claims.conditions: RP model, six-asset portfolios, 10 runs, P=5, PSO with 10 iterations
speedup_claims.caveats: Paper notes quantum methods underperform classical methods on portfolios 7-8; no asymptotic speedup is claimed.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Not explicitly characterized asymptotically; circuit depth P increases and cost/runtime grow exponentially with P as stated qualitatively

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Would require scaling QAOAz circuits to much larger asset universes (>>6 qubits) and running on fault‑tolerant hardware capable of deep variational circuits with many parameter updates.
limiting_factors: Experiments run only on noiseless simulation using Cirq
Problem size limited to 6 assets (≈6 logical qubits)
No asymptotic complexity advantage proven for QAOA/QAOAz in portfolio optimization
Hybrid optimizer cost dominated by classical PSO iterations
Quartic Hamiltonian terms increase circuit complexity for larger portfolios

notes: hardware.type inferred as simulator_other because the paper states the code uses Cirq and reports no specific QPU or simulator backend; no gate-based hardware device is named.
num_qubits inferred from the six-asset portfolio instances and binary selection variables x_i for each asset.
speedup_order marked none_proven because the paper provides empirical comparisons and qualitative scaling remarks but no asymptotic quantum speedup claim.
The paper claims 'performance advantages over classical algorithms' based on objective values, but experiments are performed on 6‑asset toy portfolios in simulation.
No hardware execution or asymptotic speedup analysis is provided.

experiments.description: PSO-optimized QAOAz for mean-variance (MV) portfolio optimization on six-asset Chinese A-share portfolios; compared against QAOA and QAOAz baselines.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Alternating Operator Ansatz (QAOAz) with ring XY-mixer and PSO classical optimizer
algorithm.ansatz: QAOAz circuit with alternating problem unitary and ring XY-mixer unitary
algorithm.convergence_criteria: max_iterations=10 for PSO; circuit depth fixed at P=5
algorithm.parameter_initialization: PSO particles initialized with random positions and velocities; QAOAz parameters initialized within [0, 2π]

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Binary variable x_i indicates whether asset i is selected; constraint enforces exactly B selected assets
problem_formulation.objective_function: F_MV = q * sum_{i,j=1}^n x_i x_j σ_ij - (1-q) * sum_{i=1}^n x_i μ_i + A(sum_{i=1}^n x_i - B)^2
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Cardinality constraint handled by XY-mixer feasibility-preserving subspace; penalty term A(sum x_i - B)^2 included in formulation
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H_p derived from MV objective with Z and ZZ terms via x_i=(1+Z_i)/2

problem_instance.description: Mean-variance portfolio optimization on six Chinese A-share portfolios

dataset_specification.description: Six randomly selected stocks from the CSI-300 Composite Index for each portfolio; date range 2022-01-01 to 2022-12-31

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Covariance matrices and expected returns computed from 2022 market data; six-stock portfolios selected to fit current quantum hardware limits
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Each algorithm run 10 times; best, worst, average, standard deviation, and approximate ratio reported

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Covariance matrices and expected returns computed from market data; portfolio selection constrained to six assets
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measured bitstrings interpreted as binary asset-selection vectors; objective values and approximate ratios computed from sampled solutions

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: convergence evaluated on Portfolio 1; 10 PSO iterations deemed sufficient

speedup_claims.factor: PSO-QAOAz-MV achieves better objective values and higher AR than QAOA and QAOAz; AR up to 100%
speedup_claims.conditions: MV model, six Chinese A-share portfolios, 10 runs, P=5, PSO with 10 iterations, q=0.5
speedup_claims.caveats: Improvement is empirical on small six-asset instances; no asymptotic speedup claim.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Not explicitly characterized asymptotically; circuit depth P increases and cost/runtime grow exponentially with P as stated qualitatively

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Would require scaling QAOAz circuits to significantly larger portfolios and executing on fault‑tolerant quantum hardware with efficient variational optimization.
limiting_factors: Evaluation performed only in noiseless simulation
No demonstrated asymptotic quantum speedup over classical mean‑variance optimization
Hybrid PSO optimization dominates computational cost
Variational algorithms may suffer from scaling issues such as barren plateaus
